steps: This video shows why a deny rule always beats an allow rule. Your code builds Claude agent options once: allow Read and Grep, deny Bash, and cap the run at ten turns.
Query starts a one shot run. The S D K sends Claude the prompt, run the cleanup script, along with the tool list, while your code iterates over the streamed messages.
Claude still asks for Bash to run the cleanup script. That is the key point: allowed tools approves tools automatically, it does not hide the others from Claude.
The S D K refuses before anything runs. Bash is in disallowed tools, so Claude gets an error tool result, and the Bash tool is never called. Deny always wins over allow.
Claude turns the refusal into a helpful answer, explaining that Bash is not permitted and that it did not run the cleanup script. Nothing destructive happened.

Every run ends with a result message: one turn, a cost of under half a cent, and a resumable session id. The takeaway: allow lists approve, deny lists block, and deny wins. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
